production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.

dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer
cache at /workspace/cache when needed. Validate the actual witnesses and census
coverage, not merely a lower finding count caused by sampling or suppression.

FINAL REPORT

## 1. Confirmed cause

Issue #2903's acceptance criterion "proven-equal dynamic indices can identify the same element; proven-disjoint ranges can reject a conflict; unknown indices remain open" could not be met for two independent, structured reasons.

- Consumer gap: `IndexAliasDomain` carried `constant_index: Option<u128>`, and `canonicalize_bound_accesses` fell back to `invocation_scalar_integer`, which returned one activation's *exact* value only. A bound established by a caller or maintained across loop iterations was therefore invisible, and `access_location_overlap`'s Element arm could only compare two exact constants for equality - it had no representation for "cannot intersect".
- Producer gap: Go's increment/decrement statement was erased. `GoSemanticLowerer::increment_statement` called `append_language_defined_value_flows(builder, boundary, [old], computed)`, so `i++` never produced the arithmetic step that `ScalarStateDerivation` needs to bound a loop counter; the guard refinement on `i < N` had nothing to refine against.

Structured evidence (temporary in-tree probe, `BIFROST_DEBUG_ACCESS=1`, base vs. change, `/tmp/probe-before.log` vs `/tmp/probe-after3.log`, identical fixtures): `equalLoops` `proven=false ... index:open reasons=[UnknownLocation]` -> `proven=true exhaustive=true ... index:0`; `parameterLoopConstant` -> `index:0 proven=true`; `disjointLoops` and `zeroIterationLoop` had an open conflict -> no conflict at all; negatives unchanged and still open (`overlappingLoops`, `unknownParameter`, `parameterOtherElement`, `capturedConstant`). The probe was then deleted and replaced by nine committed regression tests.

## 2. Changes and reasons

Full base: `3427b2ad84cc0d6ebacd963182cd4f1fed8f88c8` (detached, verified as `HEAD~1`). Final commit: `bf261de549fdb99cbacee27fa41a18c4228def4e`.

- `crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/go/semantic.rs`: `increment_statement` now publishes the exact `SemanticEffect::ValueFlow { kind: ValueFlowKind::IntegerOffset { offset: SignedIntegerMagnitude::new(node.kind() == "dec_statement", 1) }, .. }` that the semantic IR already models, using tree-sitter node kind and the existing operand/binding values. `ADAPTER_VERSION` rotated `go-value-semantics-v75` -> `go-value-semantics-v76` because the same Go source now produces different semantic bytes (persisted language facts changed). One new lowering test pins both directions.
- `crates/bifrost-flow/src/concurrency.rs`: `IndexAliasDomain.index` is now `Option<ScalarIntegerInterval>` with `IndexAliasDomain::exact_index`/`interval_exact_index` (a negative exact subscript names no element). `SolveRequest::scalar_derivation` builds one bounded solution per activation, walking the caller chain outermost-first and seeding each callee from its parent's solved facts at the call point, charging `points.len()+1` to the shared concurrency work budget. `bounded_index_interval` reads the access's own point; `scalar_intervals_are_disjoint` rejects a conflict only across one identical `ScalarIntegerDomain` (an unsigned 200 and a signed -56 are the same machine value under wrap-around, so a domain mismatch stays open). `retain_reachable_accesses` drops accesses whose point the derivation proves unreachable, and `recursive_synchronization_executes_exactly_once` now uses exact-only entry facts via `exact_scalar_entry_facts`. Nine regression tests cover the positive, near-miss, and control shapes.
- `.agents/plans/go-bounded-scalar-cardinality-2903.md`: Progress, Surprises & Discoveries, Decision Log, and Outcomes & Retrospective updated as the living ExecPlan requires, including the explicit statement that #2903 is not complete.

## 6. Draft GitHub approach comment

Bounded index reasoning landed for #2903. Go's `x++`/`x--` statements were being lowered as language-defined value flows, so scalar derivation could not see the only arithmetic a loop induction variable performs; they now publish an exact signed integer offset, which rotates the Go adapter to `go-value-semantics-v76`. The concurrency solver now carries a bounded interval per element access instead of an exact-only constant and derives one scalar solution per activation, seeded from the caller's proven facts, so a bound established by a caller or maintained by a loop is visible inside the callee. Two accesses to one backing store are disjoint when their intervals cannot intersect in the same integer domain, and accesses at points the derivation proves unreachable are dropped, while unknown indices stay open with `UnknownLocation`. Nine flow regressions and one Go lowering regression cover equal dynamic indices, induction-variable equality, disjoint and overlapping ranges, zero-iteration loops, unbounded indices, distinct backing stores, mutated captures, a caller-seeded callee, and a reassigned actual. Reverting only the new consumer fails four of them, and reverting only the Go lowering fails the Go lowering test plus two induction tests. End to end, the shipped Go data-race policy reports one proven finding on a four-function witness file with the change and zero when only the new consumer is disabled, with the three near-miss functions staying open. Validation: flow 338/338, analysis 3393 passed with 123 skipped, Go-filtered usages/issues/semantic 49/23/122, rql concurrent-access filter 56/56, workspace Clippy with warnings denied, and formatting clean. This is a partial step: WaitGroup count and phase consumers, conditional protocol results such as `TryLock` and `errgroup.TryGo`, select-arm exclusivity, typed budget outcomes, and why/why-not witnesses remain open, and the pinned six-repo corpus was not re-run here.
